title: KV slab horizon allocation and microtrench repair playbook
creator: Ava Morgan
description: Problem: KV cache on GPU exhibits slow-growing fragmentation leading to wasted memory, elevated eviction churn, and occasional latency spikes during heavy continuous-batching workloads. This ticket defines an allocation strategy (horizon reservations + fractional lanes) and a background microtrench repair mechanism to reduce fragmentation without impacting tail latency. Goal: reduce effective fragmentation by >=30% on production-like workloads while keeping P99 token latency within +5% of baseline and not increasing CPU overhead by more than 10%.
acceptance_criteria: Simulated workloads show >=30% reduction in fragmentation index (per our FragmentationScore metric) compared to current slab allocator
End-to-end P99 token latency regression <=5% on continuous-batching traces
Eviction churn (evictions per 1M tokens) reduced by >=20% under steady-state workloads
No regressions in throughput for 95th percentile batch sizes
Telemetry for relocation copy bandwidth shows <15% of available GPU bandwidth during background repair windows
work_items: Implement horizon reservation layer: maintain headroom fraction based on rolling 1h sequence-length percentile and recent batch-size histogram
Fractional lane allocation: split KV pool into hot/horizon/cold fractional lanes with dynamic watermarks
Microtrench repair daemon: opportunistic small-range relocations with backoff based on GPU utilization and batching pressure
Relocation cost model: build relocation priority = (FragmentationScore * AccessWeight) / CopyCost; expose as telemetry
Batch-aware placement hints: colocate frequently co-accessed KV keys to reduce scatter during continuous batching
Integrate with compaction scheduler to avoid repairs during autoscale or high batch-concurrency windows
End-to-end simulation harness: extend current KV simulator with new allocation policies and run ensembles vs production traces
Add dashboard panels: FragmentationScore, RelocationBandwidth, EvictionChurn, ReservationUtilization
design_decisions: Choose fractional lanes over monolithic tail-slots to reduce cross-traffic during relocs; reduces peak copy storms at cost of slightly higher steady-state internal fragmentation
Prefer small, high-frequency microtrench repairs vs large compaction passes to keep continuous-batching latency stable
Use a conservative relocation cost model that factors in GPU copy kernel efficiency and impact on KV lookup latency
Expose a tunable headroom parameter per customer tier (hosted vs dedicated) so enterprise customers can prioritize isolation vs density
tradeoffs: Background relocations consume GPU copy bandwidth and some CPU scheduling; we throttle aggressively to avoid affecting inference kernels
Fractional lane reservations trade memory efficiency for predictability — at very low utilization this can leave unused capacity
Co-location hints improve batch locality but require extra metadata and more complex eviction logic
Microtrench repairs reduce long-tail fragmentation but add implementation complexity and edge-case handling for concurrent writes/reads
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: copy storms causing transient latency spikes. Mitigation: enforcement of max-relocation-bandwidth and reactive backoff when P95 latency increases
Risk: starvation of cold lane leading to eviction storms. Mitigation: periodic adaptive loans from horizon lane and min-reservation guarantees
Risk: telemetry blind spots on fragmentation. Mitigation: ship FragmentationScore and sample-level KV layout snapshots for 72h when testing
Risk: interference with autoscaler scaling events. Mitigation: pause compaction/repairs during scale-out/in and resume with smoothing window
telemetry_queries_and_dashboards: Grafana: /d/kvcache/fragmentation - FragmentationScore by pool and lane
Datadog: query eviction_churn{env:prod} | group_by(host,avg) - alert if > threshold
Tracing: sample relocation traces and correlate with P99 latency spikes
SLO checks: include eviction churn in runbook alerts for KV pressure
simulation_results_summary: Early simulator runs (2/2026) with 10M-event traces show 34% median FragmentationScore reduction under mixed chat completions workload
Peak relocation bandwidth stayed below 12% of GPU copy capacity in default config
Observed a small increase (+2%) in average CPU utilization for scheduler threads; within acceptable bounds
implementation_notes: Kernel: use cudaMemcpyAsync with stream isolation to limit interference; fall back to CPU memcpy for older drivers
Allocator: maintain per-GPU freelist shards with lane metadata to avoid global locks
Consistency: use lightweight epoch counters for safe concurrent relocations and concurrent read paths
Testing: add unit tests for relocation backoff, and end-to-end replay tests using production trace subsets
rollout_plan: Stage 0: internal smoke tests on dev cluster (1 node) - validate correctness and backoff behavior
Stage 1: canary pool (5% production kgw) with relocation_bandwidth_limit=5% and conservative headroom
Stage 2: expand canary (20%) if metrics stable for 48h; run A/B vs baseline for P99 latency and fragmentation
Stage 3: gradual rollout to all clusters with automatic tuning based on observed ReservationUtilizationPercent
